title: S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Indices (August 2026 data) — 9:00 a.m. ET, the pre-open half of a two-index house-price morning
source: EST: derived from the publisher's own stated schedule rule, read direct from a primary and corroborated three independent ways. (1) press.spglobal.com's June-2026-data release (2026-08-25-S-P-Cotality-Case-Shiller-Index-Reports-Annual-Gain-in-June-2026, fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, 90,394 bytes) states it verbatim: "The S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Indices are published on the last Tuesday of each month at 9:00 am ET." October 2026's Tuesdays are the 6th, 13th, 20th and 27th, so the last is 2026-10-27; the same release's own two-month reporting lag (published 2026-08-25, reporting June 2026) puts August 2026 data on that edition. (2) The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis publishes this release's forward calendar — fred.stlouisfed.org/releases/calendar?rid=199, fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200 — and it names "October 27, 2026" explicitly, alongside all twelve 2026 dates and all twelve 2025 dates; every one of those 24 is the last Tuesday of its month. (3) ALFRED's vintage series for CSUSHPINSA carries a distinct vintage stamped at each of those dates. A newsroom-archive discrepancy was chased down and resolved rather than inherited: press.spglobal.com's release archive lists the January-2026-data report under a 2026-04-28 URL slug and dateline with no March 2026 item, which the pending-home-sales-2026-10-20 proposal read as a missed release — but that report's own body names its release date verbatim ("...will be provided for the March 31, 2026, release date"), the 2026-03-31 ALFRED vintage exists and carries January-2026 data, and a 2026-03-31 press slug returns 404. The release happened on schedule; the archive item was re-dated. Filed `estimate`, and the reason is taxonomy rather than date doubt: CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs is (IR|CAL|BLS|FED|PJM|SEC|TSY|OCC|BEA|CENSUS|ISM|CB|UMICH|FHFA) and has no member for an index provider's own standing publication rule, while `FED:` is scoped to the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar and not to a Reserve Bank's release calendar. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE written 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, after reading both proposals that discovered it (from-nar-metro-home-prices-2026-10-29 and from-pending-home-sales-2026-10-20), which this file now shadows. It is the calendar's FIRST Case-Shiller entry of any date. Impact `low` and `symbols: []` on measured grounds, not convention: no house playbook in docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md is macro- or housing-keyed (0 hits, re-grepped 2026-09-08), no instrument attaches, and this session's own pre-open test — the one the 9:00 a.m. ET timestamp makes possible and no sibling could run — finds nothing. Across 68 release days since 2021, the |open/prev-close| gap on ITB is 0.428% against a 0.488% baseline (p=0.4090) and DHI 0.604% vs 0.596% (p=0.9291); the only near-misses are SPY (p=0.0604) and QQQ (p=0.0570), both NARROWER and both broad-market rather than housing. THE STRUCTURAL POINT FOR THE NEXT LANE: Case-Shiller, FHFA HPI and Conference Board Consumer Confidence all key on the last Tuesday, so the 68 release days measured here are the SAME 68 days the fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 ledger measured — this session reproduces its session-range table to three decimals from an independent fetch. Attribution to any one of the three publishers is not merely hard on 2026-10-27, it is unavailable on every release day either index has ever had. AUGUST DATA, AND STALER THAN IT LOOKS: the national index is a three-month moving average reported at a two-month lag, so the 10-27 print averages June-August closings and contains nothing signed after the 2026-09-16 FOMC. That construction makes it the most forecastable print on this calendar — repeating the prior month's m/m predicts it to a 0.119pp MAE against FHFA's 0.218pp (2015+, FRED CSUSHPISA vs HPIPONM226S). NAME NOTE: renamed from "S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller" to "S&P Cotality Case-Shiller"; a search on the old name misses it. An estimate widens caution; nothing here licenses an entry.
